name: feolagan

attributes.attribute: froze sheep by walking across their backs
could not eat or drink after being frozen
cure required the same feolagan to cross the back again
guilty one could be shut in a jar of salt

sources: MacGregor, Alasdair Alpin. *The Peat-Fire Flame: Folk-Tales and Traditions of the Highlands & Islands.* Edinburgh: The Moray Press, 1937, 131.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The feolagan is a Scottish folkloric figure. It is a dangerous and elusive FAIRY. It plagued shepherders, chiefly in the Hebrides. It favored the grazing land around Kebock Head, found on the Isle of Lewis. The feolagan stood larger than the common fairy. Sheep grew frozen once it crossed over their backs. The animals could not eat or drink, and soon died. One cure existed. One had to catch the very feolagan that had bewitched the sheep. That fairy had to recross the sheep's back in reverse. The wrong feolagan only deepened the paralysis. When a whole flock faltered, one could seal the offending feolagan into a salt jar. Grains taken from the jar would heal the animals.

okr.objective: The feolagan is a Scottish fairy that froze sheep and demanded a specific cure.
key_results: The feolagan plagued shepherders in the Hebrides.
It froze sheep by walking across their backs.
Only the same feolagan could lift the paralysis by crossing back again.
A great many stricken sheep led to a jar of salt.
okr.evidence: Monaghan, Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore
